title: Multiomics and Transplant Medicine – Interview with Professor Brendan Keating on Translating Proteomics
summary: The post Multiomics and Transplant Medicine – Interview with Professor Brendan Keating on Translating Proteomics appeared first on Nautilus Biotechnology .
body_markdown:
[Professor Brendan Keating’s lab](https://med.nyu.edu/faculty/brendan-keating) focuses on “advancing the field of organ transplantation” and employs multiomic techniques to improve outcomes for both allo- (human to human) and xeno- (animal to human) transplantation. He’s using[multiomics](https://www.nautilus.bio/blog/what-is-multiomics/) to better understand the mechanisms of rejection and acceptance with a particular focus on immunologic barriers in cross-species transplantation. Professor Keating joins Translating Proteomics to discuss:


- The current state of transplant medicine including xenotransplantation.
- How multiomics is changing transplant medicine.
- The future of transplant medicine.


Stream the episode on[Apple Podcasts](https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/multiomics-and-transplant-medicine/id1739213971?i=1000796406143) ,[Spotify](https://open.spotify.com/episode/2UaaktFA1qudDep8hPPGf1?si=TBkpLu4dTImVbLrrI5CEFg) , or[YouTube](https://youtu.be/AQ6CoB9EQ50) .
